findings.description: The single commit in e70c3b5..HEAD says why the change exists rather than only what moved, is one logical change, and carries no AI-writing tells or typographic violations in the venues this clause enumerates.
findings.evidence: git cat-file commit 32d2418: subject 'fix(courier): drop script-checked clauses before they cross to a courier'; body para 1 gives the cause - 'A script-checked clause runs deterministically and agrees with itself by construction, so sending it to a courier as evidence proves nothing: the far side is being asked to bless a verdict the check already produced.'; para 2 gives the reason exit 3 is distinct from the zero-clauses error; para 3 gives the reason the fixture changed rather than the filter loosening. This is the opposite of C-10's failing example, which names a subject that states the edit without the all-script task behind it. grep -c on the message: 0 em dashes, and it adds no headings. Granularity: one commit carrying the partition, its tests, and the regenerated packages C-2 requires in the same commit. Recorded as an observation, not a defect: added code comments and the module docstring use spaced em dashes (9 occurrences, e.g. 'courier to cross - distinct from 1 because it names a different problem'), but C-10's text scopes human-facing prose to 'commit messages, the #106 comment, and the doc and role text C-8 covers'; this task touched no C-8 doc and posted no comment, and the venue in question is entrenched house style - the untouched merge-base composer has 6, the constitution 30, and T-004.md's own spec excerpt 12.

(1) Mixed fixture citing script clause C-1 and judgment clause C-2 -> exit 0; grep for 'C-1' in the brief rc=1, grep for its check line 'check-build.sh' rc=1, grep -c for its text 0; a regex-extracted C-2 block from the fixture constitution is present verbatim in the brief (True).
